title: The Magic Sticks of the Qazi (PT)
summary: Birbal gives seven suspects identical bamboo sticks, claiming the thief's stick will grow two inches by morning. The thief cuts his stick and confesses.
full_text:
A wealthy merchant of Agra woke to find his iron strongbox looted of a thousand silver coins. Seven trusted household servants were the only people who had access to the inner courtyard during the night, but all seven vehemently swore their innocence.

The merchant brought the servants to Emperor Akbar's court. Akbar handed the case to Birbal.

Birbal listened to the servants, nodded thoughtfully, and retired to an anteroom. He returned carrying seven slender bamboo sticks, each cut to the exact length of twelve inches.

Birbal handed one stick to each suspect and announced with grave solemnity:

'These are enchanted bamboo rods gifted by a Tibetan hermit. Tonight, each of you shall keep his stick beneath his bed. By morning, the stick belonging to the guilty thief will magically grow by exactly two inches through mystical power! Return here at sunrise to present your sticks to the Emperor.'

The servants bowed and returned home. Six innocent servants slept peacefully throughout the night, untroubled by fear.

However, the servant who had actually stolen the money tossed and turned in terror. 'If my stick grows two inches by morning, my guilt will be glaringly obvious! What should I do?'

In the dead of night, he crept into his kitchen, took a sharp knife, and carefully sawed off exactly two inches from his bamboo stick. 'Now,' he thought smugly, 'when it grows two inches tonight, it will match the original twelve inches of the others, and I shall be safe!'

At dawn, the seven servants lined up before Emperor Akbar. Birbal collected the sticks and measured them with a brass ruler. Six sticks measured precisely twelve inches. But the thief's stick measured only ten inches!

'Arrest him!' Birbal commanded. 'The sticks were ordinary bamboo with no magic at all. But your guilty conscience shortened what you feared would grow!'

The trembling servant confessed on the spot, returned the stolen silver, and the entire court marveled at Birbal's clever trap.
